artists.biography:
No-Man are an English art-pop duo formed in 1987 as No Man Is An Island (Except The Isle Of Man) by singer Tim Bowness and multi-instrumentalist Steven Wilson (the latter also of Porcupine Tree). The band has so far produced six studio albums and a number of singles/outtakes collections (most notably, 2006's career retrospective, All The Blue Changes). The band was once lauded as "conceivably the most important English group since The Smiths" by Melody Maker music newspaper.
Originally creating a sample-based proto-trip hop/ambient/electro-pop-styled music, No-Man has pursued a more organic, diverse and band-oriented sound in subsequent years. Drawing from a diverse mix of singer-songwriter, post rock, minimalist, progressive rock, jazz and contemporary ambient sources for inspiration, No-Man's musical style is distinctive yet difficult to categorise.

perplexity.description:
Love You to Bits is the seventh studio album by No-Man, released on November 22, 2019, marking the British duo's return after an 11-year hiatus since Schoolyard Ghosts (2008). The album represents a deliberate shift toward the electronic, beat-driven sound of the band's earliest work while incorporating the conceptual and organic elements that characterized their later releases. Structured as two five-part song cycles with a total runtime of approximately 36 minutes, the album mimics a vinyl format and explores the emotional aftermath of a relationship breakdown from multiple perspectives.

Musically, Love You to Bits combines electronic loops, atmospheric textures, and rhythmic elements that invite both contemplative listening and physical response. Tim Bowness's vocals anchor the album, conveying emotional detachment and melancholy, while Steven Wilson contributes background harmonies that complement the primary narrative. The production, handled by No-Man and mixed by Bruno Ellingham, incorporates contributions from jazz guitarist David Kollar and other session musicians, creating a sonically layered work that balances accessibility with artistic ambition.

The album received positive critical reception for its willingness to push the band's musical boundaries while maintaining their distinctive identity. Reviewers noted its listenable yet intricate construction, with the dual song cycles creating thematic and sonic coherence throughout the work. Released through Caroline International/Universal, Love You to Bits demonstrated that No-Man remained creatively vital despite their extended absence from recording.
